script.base: Working hypothesis, not a market-implied forecast: DAL's passing production gives it a plausible route to a narrow lead, while HOU can remain competitive by attacking DAL's vulnerable run defense. A competitive game preserves receiving opportunities for C.Lamb and D.Schultz; pace, halftime leadership and garbage time cannot be established from this pack.
script.flip1: HOU controls possession through its running game against DAL's 5.23 YPC allowed and 15 runs allowed of 10-plus yards. Lamb can retain comeback opportunities, but Schultz's receiving volume becomes script-dependent if HOU needs fewer passes.
script.flip2: DAL builds an early multi-score lead and shifts toward J.Williams, who has 43 carries across weeks 1–3. Lamb's yardage opportunity can stall, while Schultz could retain catch-up volume; neither over is insulated against every script.

Schultz leads HOU with 25 targets and 205 receiving yards, with 157 air yards; Hutchinson follows with 21 targets, 120 receiving yards and 290 air yards. These aggregates support current involvement but cannot reveal weekly consistency, snap or route trends, red-zone usage, long-play dependence, play-caller changes or results against comparable defenses.

data_check.notes: The hypotheses were formed from roles and defensive vulnerabilities before comparing the lines. Subsequent arithmetic checks: Lamb's three-game receiving total implies 103.0 yards per game versus 76.5; Schultz's implies 68.3 versus 40.5. Those aggregates support plausibility, not hit probabilities or projections. Lamb over -114 requires 53.27% to break even; Schultz over -113 requires 53.05%. No projection or simulation was run, and no quantified positive expected value is established. Both remain conditional leans.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both overs lost: HOU successfully ran against DAL's 5.23 YPC allowance, shortened the game and reduced Schultz's opportunities, while Lamb's routes encountered HOU's stronger left-side coverage or DAL's passing efficiency deteriorated against pressure. The pack does not establish where either player runs routes, and three-game totals can conceal a single inflated performance. Lamb's target competition from Pickens and Schultz's competition from Hutchinson further weaken any assumption of guaranteed volume. These counterarguments keep both reads at lean rather than strong.
slip_story: Both candidates fit one competitive-game story: DAL generates passing production through Lamb while HOU continues involving Schultz. Lamb survives a HOU-led comeback script better; Schultz survives a DAL-led catch-up script better. Do not force a 3–4-leg slip from this game: only two conditional candidates qualify, and their shared script and joint price have not been modeled. No TDs, depth-receiver additions or second market on either player.
